title: Few-Shot Prompting & Dynamic In-Context Learning
description: Master static and dynamic few-shot learning, exemplar selection, edge-case demonstrations, and vector-backed example retrieval in C#.

data.text: When foundational models are instructed in a zero-shot manner (simply describing what to do), they often misunderstand subtle nuances or format preferences. Few-shot prompting provides the model with concrete input-output demonstration pairs (exemplars) directly inside the prompt context. Through in-context learning, the transformer's attention heads calibrate to the demonstrated pattern without updating any neural weights.

data.title: Exemplar Design Principles
items: Demonstrate Boundary Cases: Include examples that demonstrate how the model should behave when an input is ambiguous, malformed, or missing required keys.
Keep Examples Diverse: Avoid redundant examples that demonstrate the exact same pattern; cover distinct variations in input phrasing and complexity.
Maintain Consistent Delimiters: Use uniform prefixes (Input: / Output:) across all demonstrations so the model recognizes where generation must begin.
Order Sensitivity: Place the most challenging or representative example last, as recent tokens in the context window exert strong attention bias.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Few-shot prompting drastically reduces formatting failures and edge-case errors through in-context learning
Static few-shot embeds fixed examples; dynamic few-shot retrieves semantically relevant examples from a vector database
Always include boundary and negative examples showing how to respond to ambiguous or invalid inputs
Exemplar order matters: recent examples exert higher attention weight in the model's self-attention layers
Dynamic few-shot prompting is particularly effective for code, SQL, and complex domain-specific transformations
data.takeaway: Showing is superior to telling in prompt engineering. By supplying high-quality, targeted exemplars, .NET developers guide models toward consistent, enterprise-grade output accuracy.
